docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The small Latin book of March 1610 in which Galileo announced the first telescopic observations of the sky: the rough surface of the Moon, the many faint stars of the Milky Way and the nebulae, and four bodies moving around Jupiter. In the English of Edward Stafford Carlos (1880), with the introduction of the translator and the continuation by Kepler.

From Wikisource · Public domain

Galileo Galilei (1564–1642), Sidereus nuncius (Latin), 1610, translated by Edward Stafford Carlos (1842–1927), 1880; text from Wikisource.
